sections.html:
Saline County's seat is Benton, a Little Rock-North Little Rock-Conway metro suburb whose population climbed from 21,906 in 2000 to 30,681 in 2010 and 35,014 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate is 38,898. In 2020 the city counted 14,785 housing units, 7.1 percent of them vacant.

Older small frame houses stand beside newer subdivisions, a legacy of early trades like a salt works and kaolin pottery. Commuters reach Little Rock on Interstate 30 and Interstate 530, and U.S. Highways 65, 67, 70 and 167 and Arkansas Highways 5, 9 and 35 also cross the county. A short drive to an interchange is a selling point, so put it in writing when you talk to a buyer.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
The Benton School District, which feeds Benton High School, covers most of town. A few other districts reach into the area, so your exact address decides it.

  • Benton School District: most of the city.
  • Bryant Public Schools: nearby addresses, with Bryant High School.
  • Bauxite School District: the Bauxite end of the county.
  • Harmony Grove School District: a small southeast pocket near Frontage Road, with Benton Harmony Grove High School.

Look up the district for your street before advertising, because families ask right away. A house on a boundary line can draw a different crowd than one a few blocks over.

sections.h2: Wet weather and what buyers check
sections.html:
Heat, moisture and rain, not snow, wear on a Benton house. July daily highs average about 92.9 degrees Fahrenheit, and the year brings roughly 53 inches of rain over about 74 days. Inspectors and appraisers tend to focus on four things.

  • Roof condition and past leaks, since long wet seasons find weak flashing.
  • Crawl space moisture, soft wood and sagging floors.
  • Air conditioner age, because summers are long and hot.
  • Gutters, grading and drainage around the foundation.

A long repair list slows a traditional sale. A buyer paying cash for the house as is does not require you to fix them first.

At City Hall, 410 River Street, the Community Development office issues building permits and enforces codes. It posts forms for residential remodels, accessory buildings, swimming pools, fences, retaining walls, grading, demolition and house moving, plus floodplain forms. Staff answer 501-776-5938 from 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, and permit submissions go to permits@bentonar.gov.

The code team looks at overgrown lots, standing water and abandoned or inoperable vehicles. Parking a boat, trailer, farm implement or vehicle on public property for more than seven consecutive days is a public nuisance, unless it is inside a building or connected to a business.

  • Open permits or unpermitted additions, decks and carports.
  • Code complaints for tall grass or stored vehicles.
  • Whether the lot sits in a mapped flood area, which would involve the floodplain forms.

An unresolved violation or an unpermitted project can raise questions during a buyer's inspection. A cash sale as is spares you the cure, but tell the buyer what you know.

The bill comes a year late. Saline County sends it to whoever owned the house on the assessment date. Collector offices in Benton and Bryant keep weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the main line is 501-303-5620. A payment by mail needs an October 15 postmark.

sections.h2: Questions to settle before you list
sections.html:
A few quick calls can save weeks. Phone the collector at 501-303-5620 and ask for the balance on your parcel. Phone Community Development at 501-776-5938 and ask whether any permit is still open on the property. Look up your street on the school district boundary and write down the answer.

Then walk the house the way an inspector would. Check the roof for stained decking, look under the sink and in the crawl space for dampness, and run the air conditioner. Fix cheap items, and be ready to name the expensive ones. A buyer who hears about a problem from you rarely treats it as a surprise. Take dated photos of the house as it stands today, including any damage you have not repaired, so that you and the buyer agree on the condition at the time of the offer. Keep receipts for repairs you did complete, since they show the work was done and when.

A new countywide reappraisal sent out its first notices in July 2026. Owners get one only if their value rose. The letter is not a bill, and the higher figure stays off this October's payment. If it looks wrong, call the assessor, and if that fails, ask the county equalization board to hear it. Keep the notice with your closing paperwork, because a buyer may want to see it.

sections.h2: Property tax and the closing statement
sections.html:
Your contract and the settlement statement set how seller and buyer divide the year's bill, so have the title company show the tax line. The state also levies a real property transfer tax, $3.30 per $1,000 of the sale price, on transfers above $100. Who pays it is a matter for the purchase contract.

If you still live in the house, the homestead credit applies. The Benton County assessor puts the statewide credit at up to $600 off the tax bill on a primary residence, and Saline County's assessor can confirm how it works for your parcel.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Benton
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company searches the Saline County record for unpaid tax, liens and recorded problems. Have your last tax statement, deed and permit paperwork ready, and mention any open code complaint so it does not surprise anyone. If you are selling an inherited house, bring the documents that show who owns it now.

The closing meeting is mostly signing. The deed is recorded with the county, the tax balance and any lien are paid out of what you receive, and you leave with the remainder. Without a lender's appraisal in the way, a clean search can mean a date you pick.

Before you accept, ask for the offer in writing and compare the amount you would net after payoff, repairs and carrying costs against a listing. Ask who pays the recording fee and the state transfer tax, and confirm the answer in the contract.

sections.h2: Taking the house as it stands
sections.html:
Plenty of Benton houses are well loved but dated. Original windows, a tired kitchen or an air conditioner near the end of its life do not stop a sale, they change who the buyer is. A family with a lender wants the repairs finished. An investor paying cash expects to do them and prices the house to match.

If you lean toward a cash sale, ask each buyer the same questions. When can you close? Is the offer in writing? Who pays the title and recording costs? Does the price depend on an inspection? Plain answers tell you more than a high number that can shrink later.

sections.h2: What Benton sellers usually run into
sections.html:
Common situations include a parent's house now owned by several heirs, a rental with tenants and deferred repairs, an owner behind on a mortgage or tax bill, and a seller who wants to skip showings.

The timelines differ. Listing the house means repairs, showings, a buyer's lender and an appraisal. Selling for cash to an investor lets you pick the closing date, and the buyer inherits the repairs. Weigh the net amount and the schedule for each.

faqs.q: Is Benton the county seat of Saline County?
faqs.a: Yes, and the Saline County Courthouse stands downtown. Deeds for Benton houses are recorded with the county.

faqs.q: When are Saline County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 15 is the last day. Payments start March 1, and unpaid balances after October 15 take a 10 percent penalty. Mail must be postmarked by that date.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit or inspection to sell my Benton house?
faqs.a: The sale itself does not need one, but work on the house should have been permitted. Call Community Development at 501-776-5938 to ask about past remodels, fences or pools.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Benton house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Open issues can complicate a regular sale, while a cash buyer will usually take the house as it stands. Ask code enforcement what is open on your address.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Benton house in?
faqs.a: Most are in the Benton School District, but some fall in Bryant, Bauxite or Harmony Grove. Look up your street before you list.
